title: Microsoft Purview: Data Security Triage Agent for DLP alerts reaches general availability
summary: The roadmap facts, deployment controls, licensing and SCU costs are supported. Minor corrections should acknowledge additional disagreements between the cited Learn pages and identify the checklist's Teams app-permissions control as missing from the controls table.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Governance controls table
claims.claim: A tenant can have only one instance of this agent.
claims.quote: There can be only one instance of each agent in a tenant, regardless of the portal in which it was deployed.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Remediation reminders in Teams are preview.
claims.quote: Remediation reminder (Preview)

claims.claim: The reminder-duration setting is preview.
claims.quote: Reminder duration (Preview)

claims.claim: Usage monitoring tracks consumption rather than imposing a consumption limit.
claims.quote: The usage monitoring dashboard provides a comprehensive view into various data dimensions to help you keep track of Security Compute Units (SCUs) usage in Security Copilot.

claims.claim: This is a Microsoft Security Copilot agent embedded in Purview Data Loss Prevention.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview offers: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) triage agent ... You can find these agents in the Microsoft Purview embedded experiences.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The agent reads the content behind DLP alerts, including files and messages.
claims.quote: Running this logic against the alert content associated with each alert. ... The Triage agent in DLP triages alerts from Exchange, Devices, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams.

claims.claim: The Needs attention category contains alerts judged to pose the greatest risk.
claims.quote: Needs attention: This category contains alerts that the agent evaluated and determined pose the greatest risk to your organization.

claims.claim: The Less urgent category contains alerts judged to pose a lower risk.
claims.quote: Less Urgent: These less urgent results are the alerts the agent evaluated and determined to pose a lower risk to your organization.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Not categorized contains alerts the agent could not successfully triage.
claims.quote: Not categorized: Uncategorized results are the alerts that the agent wasn't able to successfully triage

claims.claim: The agent supplies summaries explaining its categorisation decisions.
claims.quote: The agent offers a comprehensive explanation for the logic behind the categorization.

claims.claim: Supported DLP policy locations are Exchange, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint and devices.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Purview Triage Agent in DLP triages alerts from policies that are scoped to Exchange, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, and devices (Endpoint) locations, only.

claims.claim: The agent triages only active-mode policies, not simulation-mode policies.
claims.quote: The Triage agent in DLP only supports alerts from policies that are in active mode. It doesn't triage alerts from DLP policies that are running in simulation mode.

claims.claim: Triaging device alerts requires evidence collection for file activities on devices to be enabled.
claims.quote: If you want to triage alerts from devices, Evidence collection for file activities on devices must be enabled.

claims.claim: The agent triages files up to 2 MB.
claims.quote: Agents triage files up to 2 MB in size.

claims.claim: For alerts with 10 or more files, the agent uses the top 10 to produce the file risk summary.
claims.quote: When an alert includes 10 or more files, the agent uses the potentially top 10 files to generate the file risk summary.

claims.claim: Results appear in the Purview solution's Alerts page in the Triage Agent view.
claims.quote: Open the Alerts page for the solution. ... Set the toggle to the Triage Agent view. This view shows agent triaged alerts.

claims.claim: Agent summaries also appear on triaged DLP alerts in Defender XDR.
claims.quote: Agent-provided summaries and risk factors will be available on DLP alerts triaged by the Agent as they are in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: Deployment is available from both Purview and Defender XDR.
claims.quote: The Triage Agent can be deployed from both Microsoft Purview and Defender XDR portals

claims.claim: The agent can be managed, edited and disabled only in Purview.
claims.quote: but can only be managed, edited, and disabled from the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The agent starts within 30–60 minutes after setup.
claims.quote: After setup is complete, the agent starts running within 30–60 minutes and begins triaging DLP alerts.

claims.claim: By default, it processes all DLP policies' alerts generated in the past 30 days.
claims.quote: By default, the agent processes alerts from all DLP policies generated within the past 30 days.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The agent can run using a dedicated Microsoft Entra agent identity.
claims.quote: Create and use agent identity (recommended): Create a separate Microsoft Entra agent identity for the agent. Associate all agent activities with this agent identity.
claims.fix: Add to the existing source-disagreement paragraph: 'The older preview page also says the DLP agent runs as the administrator who enabled it and that authentication expires after 90 days, whereas the get-started page now documents an agent-identity option.' The older statement is at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/copilot-in-purview-agents; the new option is at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/copilot-in-purview-triage-dlp-agent-get-started.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Alternatively, the agent can run as the user or administrator who sets it up.
claims.quote: Assign and use my identity: Set up the agent by using the identity of the user or admin who sets up the agent. Associate all activities with the user's identity.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends agent identity and migration from user identity.
claims.quote: Regarding an agent that that was set up using a user's identity, migration to the agent identity in agent settings is recommended.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The identity settings can be changed later through deployment configuration.
claims.quote: These settings can be changed anytime by visiting the deployment configurations tab for the agent in Explore agents page.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: When agent identity is used, the agent is assigned Data classification content viewer.
claims.quote: These roles are assigned to the Triage agent in DLP when agent identity is used: ... Data classification content viewer (needed to get the contextual summary)

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: When agent identity is used, the agent is assigned Data classification content downloader for endpoint evidence.
claims.quote: These roles are assigned to the Triage agent in DLP when agent identity is used: ... Data classification content downloader (needed for endpoint scenario)

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[1]; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The person deploying the agent chooses its look-back timeframe.
claims.quote: Select the alert timeframe, which is how far back the agent looks for alerts to triage.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[1]; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The agent's policy scope is configurable.
claims.quote: Specify the policy scope of the triage agent to control which DLP policy alerts and which policies are eligible for remediation reminders.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[1]; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The person deploying the agent can choose whether it sends remediation reminders in Teams.
claims.quote: Enable Remediation reminders in Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: Admins and analysts with the setup roles can deploy the agent from the one-click banner using default settings.
claims.quote: Any admin or analyst for a tenant (with no agent deployed) sees a banner or card on alerts page for Triage agent setup. Select Start agent to deploy and enable the agent. The roles needed for this setup align with the roles mentioned previously for normal setup flow.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: One-click deployment uses automatic scheduled execution by default.
claims.quote: The default settings for 'One-Click' setup are: ... Trigger: Run automatically based on a set schedule

claims.claim: One-click setup leaves remediation reminders off.
claims.quote: The default settings for 'One-Click' setup are: ... Remediation reminder: Turned OFF (Preview)

claims.claim: E5 and E7 inclusion uses Default Security Copilot Capacity shared across all tenant users and experiences.
claims.quote: Default Security Copilot Capacity is the automatically created inclusion capacity that appears in your tenant when Security Copilot inclusion is enabled through Microsoft 365 E5 and E7. ... It's shared across all users and experiences in the tenant

claims.claim: Microsoft says agents are not administrative-unit aware.
claims.quote: Agents aren't administrative unit aware.

claims.claim: An unrestricted agent identity is not confined to one administrative unit's alerts.
claims.quote: Agents aren't administrative unit aware. But if the agent runs in the context of an administrative-unit restricted admin, and there are policies that are administrative-unit scoped to that admin, the agent only sees alerts from the policies that scoped to the admin unit.

claims.claim: Microsoft sets the run schedule rather than the organisation configuring it.
claims.quote: Microsoft sets the schedule and it isn't configurable by organizations.

claims.claim: In automatic mode, the agent categorises alerts without an analyst reviewing them first.
claims.quote: If you select Run automatically based on a set schedule, the agent triages the alerts that are included in the Select Alert timeframe setting.

claims.claim: Analysts can give feedback to raise or lower alert priority.
claims.quote: If the initial value is Needs attention, you can change it to Less urgent. If the initial categorization is Less urgent, you can reprioritize it as Needs attention.

claims.claim: Custom instructions are preview.
claims.quote: Custom instructions (Preview)

claims.claim: Saved custom instructions affect future triage.
claims.quote: Once the instruction is saved, the agent uses it to triage all future alerts.

claims.claim: Feedback can apply to the triggering policy or all policies.
claims.quote: If you want to Apply the feedback to all policies, select that option. Otherwise, the feedback is applied only to the policy that triggered the alert.

claims.claim: Enabled reminders message the last modifier of SharePoint or OneDrive files in Needs attention alerts.
claims.quote: For Sharepoint/OneDrive alerts triaged as Needs Attention, the agent sends a Microsoft Teams chat to the last modified user of the file

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Reminders require the Teams admin center to allow the Data Security Triage Agent app to send messages.
claims.quote: To use the Remediation Capability of the Triage Agent in Data Loss Prevention, you must configure the Microsoft Teams Admin Center to allow the Data Security Triage Agent app to send messages to users.

claims.claim: Reminders are not sent when tenant Teams settings block deployment of new Teams apps.
claims.quote: If your organization's settings for Microsoft Teams do not allow the deployment of new Microsoft Teams apps, the Remediation reminders will not be sent to users in your organization.

claims.claim: Enabling remediation reminders also enables the bot in Teams for the tenant.
claims.quote: Enabling this setting also enables the bot in Microsoft Teams for the tenant.

claims.claim: SCUs must be provisioned for the agent to work.
claims.quote: You must have SCUs provisioned for the triage agent to work.

claims.claim: SCU consumption depends on the number and type of alerts processed.
claims.quote: The number of SCUs consumed depends on the number and type of alerts that are processed.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a per-alert SCU figure for this DLP agent.
claims.quote: Searched: Triage agent SCU per alert Data Loss Prevention consumption. Opened learn.microsoft.com/purview/copilot-in-purview-triage-dlp-agent-get-started, learn.microsoft.com/copilot/security/manage-usage and security-compute-units-capacity. No DLP per-alert rate found.

claims.claim: The usage page lists generally available capabilities as charged.
claims.quote: Generally available (GA) | Yes

claims.claim: The usage page lists public-preview capabilities as charged.
claims.quote: Public preview | Yes

claims.claim: E5 and E7 inclusion provides 400 SCUs monthly per 1,000 paid user licences.
claims.quote: Customers with Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 will have 400 Security Compute Units (SCU) each month for every 1,000 paid user license

claims.claim: The included allocation is up to 10,000 SCUs monthly at no additional cost.
claims.quote: up to 10,000 SCUs each month at no additional cost.

claims.claim: The included SCU allowance resets monthly.
claims.quote: SCU allocations reset monthly and don't roll over if unused.

claims.claim: Microsoft says usage beyond the included SCUs will be throttled at a future date.
claims.quote: Usage beyond the allocated SCUs will be throttled at a future date.

claims.claim: At that time customers can buy additional capacity at $6 USD per SCU pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: Customers have an option to scale beyond the allocated amount at $6 USD for each SCU on a pay-as-you go basis at that time.

claims.claim: Microsoft promises 30 days' advance notification when the additional-capacity option becomes available.
claims.quote: Customers will get a 30-day advanced notification when this option is available.

claims.claim: Provisioned SCUs for other tenants are billed hourly.
claims.quote: Provisioned capacity is billed per hour and is best for steady, predictable usage.

claims.claim: When provisioned SCUs run out, requests stop unless another capacity type is available.
claims.quote: If provisioned SCUs run out, Security Copilot requests stop unless another capacity type is available

claims.claim: Overage capacity can be configured with a maximum or set to unlimited.
claims.quote: Can be configured with a maximum limit or set to unlimited

claims.claim: Overage units are changed in Security Copilot > Settings > Owner settings > Number of overage units > Change.
claims.quote: Sign in to Security Copilot (https://securitycopilot.microsoft.com) and go to Settings. ... Through the owner settings page: Under Security compute units or Number of overage units, select Change.

claims.claim: Overage capacity allows continued use after provisioned units are depleted and incurs usage-based charges.
claims.quote: you can set an overage amount to ensure that extra SCUs are available when initially provisioned units are depleted during unexpected workload spikes. Overage units are billed on-demand

claims.claim: Preview remediation reminders cost nothing extra beyond the SCUs used to triage the alert.
claims.quote: The Remediation Capability doesn't cost anything extra. The only costs associated with using this capability are the SCUs needed to triage the DLP alert first.

claims.claim: DLP admins with the listed setup roles can deploy and configure the agent.
claims.quote: Assign these roles for setting up the agent using an recommended agent identity, actions like configuring or customizing, or deactivating and removing agents: For admins (any one from each group)

claims.claim: Analysts with the required roles can view results, give feedback and manually run the agent on single alerts.
claims.quote: The account you use to view results along with update triggers, give feedback, or custom instruction ... must be assigned the roles (any one from each group) ... you can select the alert and then select Run agent to manually run the agent on the alert.

claims.claim: Each function requires one role from each group listed for it on the get-started page.
claims.quote: For admins (any one from each group): ... For analysts (any one from each group): ... The account you use to view results ... must be assigned the roles (any one from each group)
claims.fix: Add after the role statement: 'The older preview page gives a different DLP role list: Insider Risk Management Analysts, Insider Risk Management Investigators or Insider Risk Management for viewing, plus Purview Content Analyst for management; the get-started page gives the function-specific groups referenced here.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/copilot-in-purview-agents for the older list.

claims.where: Scope: Who uses it; Governance controls
claims.claim: Security Copilot Contributor or Purview Copilot Workspace Contributor is required as one of the permission groups.
claims.quote: Group B ... Security Copilot Contributor ... Purview Copilot Workspace Contributor ... Group C ... Security Copilot Contributor ... Purview Copilot Workspace Contributor

claims.claim: The tenant must be onboarded to Security Copilot.
claims.quote: Your tenant must be onboarded to Microsoft Security Copilot.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 data sharing must be enabled in Security Copilot.
claims.quote: You must enable Microsoft 365 data sharing in Security Copilot.

claims.claim: The Purview plug-in must be enabled in Security Copilot.
claims.quote: You must enable the Microsoft Purview plug-in in Microsoft Security Copilot.

claims.where: Scope: Alerts in scope; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Policies with unsupported conditions show Limited eligibility and may have alerts the agent does not triage.
claims.quote: If a policy has some unsupported conditions--a state called limited eligibility--the Microsoft Purview DLP triage agent might not be able to triage all the alerts from that policy.

claims.claim: The Insider Risk Management triage agent is a separate agent.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview offers: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) triage agent; Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management triage agent

claims.claim: Deactivating the agent stops alert triage.
claims.quote: Deactivating the agent stops the agent from triaging alerts.

claims.claim: Deactivation does not remove the agent.
claims.quote: It doesn't remove the agent

claims.claim: Deactivation preserves the alert-timeframe reference point.
claims.quote: it doesn't reset the Select alert timeframe reference point in time.

claims.claim: Remove agent on the same ellipsis menu deletes the agent.
claims.quote: select Agents. Select Explore agents. Select Go to agent for the agent you want to remove. ... select the ellipses (three dots) ... Select Remove agent. Removing the agent deletes it from Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: Only triage new alerts is an available timeframe option.
claims.quote: If Only triage new alerts is selected, the agent only triages alerts that are generated after the agent is deployed.

claims.claim: Changing SCUs in the Security Copilot portal requires an Azure capacity owner or contributor who is also a Security Copilot owner.
claims.quote: Security Copilot portal required role: Azure capacity owner or contributor who are also Security Copilot owners.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist's instruction to agree Teams app permissions has a corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Leave Remediation reminders in Microsoft Teams off until the Teams app permissions and user communication are agreed. | The five control rows cover deployment, agent configuration, deactivation, SCU monitoring and Purview role groups; none covers Teams app permissions.
claims.fix: Identify the missing control in Governance controls with: 'The checklist also calls for checking Teams app permissions; those permissions are not represented in this table.' Do not add a control row as part of this correction.

claims.claim: Custom instructions can raise or lower alert priority.
claims.quote: Raising or lowering the alert’s priority if the content matches your custom instruction.
claims.fix: Add to the existing source-disagreement paragraph: 'The overview describes custom instructions as content-only and raising priority, while the get-started page describes content- and metadata-based instructions that can raise or lower priority.' The differing overview is https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/copilot-in-purview-agents-overview; the current detailed description is https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/copilot-in-purview-triage-dlp-agent-get-started.

claims.claim: The cited Microsoft Security Copilot agents in Purview page still labels the DLP agent preview.
claims.quote: Alert Triage Agent in Data Loss Prevention (preview)

claims.claim: The get-started page describes content risk using Microsoft-provided SITs, unlike the roadmap's expanded custom-SIT coverage.
claims.quote: Content Risk: This category is the primary risk factor used during agent triage, it covers sensitive content based on Microsoft provided sensitive information types (SIT), trainable classifiers, and default sensitivity labels.
